Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- The section never calls sdk.call, except "Vera.Ask.text" as said below: what the phone does is not its job.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them.
- If the section cannot really do it with this language and these components -- it needs a camera, a live feed, the person's location or data the phone does not hold -- decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it with made-up data.
- Suggestions, ideas, recipes, tips or questions made FROM WHAT THE PERSON ENTERED (dinners from the items in their pantry, questions from their notes, a plan from the times they set) are written by the model while the app runs, never by the section: a fixed sentence with their words pasted in ("Roast vegetable tray, uses Spinach") is not a suggestion. The section has a button that asks, a "pending" text while it waits, and the answer shown as text:
    function suggest(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
      sdk.call("Vera.Ask.text", ["prompt", "Two quick dinners using: " + names + ". One line each.", "maxWords", "60"], "onSuggested");
      return {c_ideas: "Thinking..."__PASSTHROUGH__};
    }
    function onSuggested(state: AppState, value: string): AppState { return {c_ideas: value__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  An answer starting with "error" is shown as a failure the person can try again. Call it only from a button's handler, never from view() or a ticker; and never for numbers the app works out itself or for anything known when the app is made.

</classes>
<fields>
</fields>
<functions>
function c_morning(state: AppState): number {
  let n: number = 0;
  for (let e: LogEntry of state.entries) {
    if (e.minute < 720) { n = n + 1; }
  }
  return n;
}

function c_afternoon(state: AppState): number {
  let n: number = 0;
  for (let e: LogEntry of state.entries) {
    if (e.minute >= 720 && e.minute < 1080) { n = n + 1; }
  }
  return n;
}

function c_evening(state: AppState): number {
  let n: number = 0;
  for (let e: LogEntry of state.entries) {
    if (e.minute >= 1080) { n = n + 1; }
  }
  return n;
}
</functions>
<view>
{
  let c_total: number = state.entries.length();
  if (c_total === 0) {
    sections.push(ui.Section("content", "", "", [ui.Text("caption", "Morning, afternoon and evening counts appear here once you log a headache.")]));
  } else {
    sections.push(ui.Section("content", "", "", [
      ui.SectionHeader("default", "By time of day", "When headaches start", ui.numberToString(c_total)),
      ui.MetricGroup("default", 3, [
        ui.NumberStat("default", "Morning", c_morning(state), "", "", 1, "before noon", "clock"),
        ui.NumberStat("default", "Afternoon", c_afternoon(state), "", "", 1, "noon to 6pm", "clock"),
        ui.NumberStat("default", "Evening", c_evening(state), "", "", 1, "6pm to midnight", "clock")
      ])
    ]));
  }
}
</view>

needs: A starter list of restaurant choices the person can pick from at random, such as pizza place, sushi bar, taco stand, burger joint, noodle house, and salad cafe. The person can add their own restaurants to the list and remove ones they don't want.

c_guesses: string[] = []
c_marks: string[] = []
c_input: string = ""
c_round: number = 0
c_message: string = ""
</fields>
<functions>
function c_pickWord(seed: number): string {
  let words: string[] = ["apple", "brave", "crane", "dwell", "eagle", "flame", "grape", "house", "ivory", "jolly", "knife", "lemon", "mango", "noble", "ocean", "piano", "queen", "river", "stone", "tiger", "unity", "vivid", "wheat", "youth", "zebra"];
  let n: number = words.length();
  let idx: number = math.randomBelow(seed, n);
  return words[idx];
}

function c_markGuess(word: string, guess: string): string {
  let result: string = "";
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < 5) {
    let g: string = strings.substring(guess, i, i + 1);
    let w: string = strings.substring(word, i, i + 1);
    if (g === w) {
      result = result + "c";
    } else {
      let found: boolean = false;
      let j: number = 0;
      while (j < 5) {
        let wj: string = strings.substring(word, j, j + 1);
        if (wj === g) {
          found = true;
        }
        j = j + 1;
      }
      if (found) {
        result = result + "p";
      } else {
        result = result + "a";
      }
    }
    i = i + 1;
  }
  return result;
}

function c_start(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let seed: number = time.nowMillis() + state.c_round * 7919;
  let w: string = c_pickWord(seed);
  let empty: string[] = [];
  return {c_word: w, c_guesses: empty, c_marks: empty, c_input: "", c_round: state.c_round + 1, c_message: ""__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_setInput(state: AppState, value: string): AppState {
  return {c_input: value__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_submit(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  if (state.c_word === "") {
    return {c_message: "Start a round first."__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  if (state.c_guesses.length() >= 5) {
    return {c_message: "The round is over. Start a new round."__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  let g: string = strings.toLowerCase(strings.trim(state.c_input));
  if (strings.length(g) !== 5) {
    return {c_message: "Enter a five-letter word."__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  let mark: string = c_markGuess(state.c_word, g);
  let newGuesses: string[] = [];
  for (let old: string of state.c_guesses) {
    newGuesses.push(old);
  }
  newGuesses.push(g);
  let newMarks: string[] = [];
  for (let old: string of state.c_marks) {
    newMarks.push(old);
  }
  newMarks.push(mark);
  let msg: string = "";
  if (g === state.c_word) {
    msg = "You got it!";
  } else if (newGuesses.length() >= 5) {
    msg = "Out of tries. The word was " + state.c_word + ".";
  }
  return {c_guesses: newGuesses, c_marks: newMarks, c_input: "", c_message: msg__PASSTHROUGH__};
}
</functions>

let c_over: boolean = state.c_guesses.length() >= 5 || (state.c_word !== "" && state.c_guesses.length() > 0 && state.c_guesses[state.c_guesses.length() - 1] === state.c_word);
let c_rows: ui.View[] = [];
let c_gi: number = 0;
while (c_gi < state.c_guesses.length()) {
  let c_g: string = state.c_guesses[c_gi];
  let c_m: string = state.c_marks[c_gi];
  let c_cells: ui.View[] = [];
  let c_li: number = 0;
  while (c_li < 5) {
    let c_letter: string = strings.toUpperCase(strings.substring(c_g, c_li, c_li + 1));
    let c_mk: string = strings.substring(c_m, c_li, c_li + 1);
    let c_style: string = "default";

    if (c_mk === "p") { c_style = "accent"; }
    if (c_mk === "a") { c_style = "danger"; }

    c_li = c_li + 1;

}
let c_remaining: number = 5 - state.c_guesses.length();
let c_status: string = "";
if (state.c_word === "") {
  c_status = "Tap Start to begin a round.";
} else if (c_over) {
  c_status = "Round over. The word was " + strings.toUpperCase(state.c_word) + ".";
} else {
  c_status = ui.numberToString(c_remaining) + " tries left.";
}
sections.push(ui.Section("hero", "Round", c_status, [
  ui.When(state.c_word === "", ui.ActionBar("center", [
    ui.Button("primary", "Start round", "c_start", 0, true)
  ])),
  ui.When(state.c_word !== "" && !c_over, ui.Column("default", [
    ui.TextField("default", "Your guess", state.c_input, "c_setInput", "", true, "Enter a five-letter word.", 5, "Use exactly five letters.", 5, "Use exactly five letters."),
    ui.ActionBar("end", [
      ui.Button("primary", "Submit guess", "c_submit", 0, true)
    ])
  ])),
  ui.When(c_over, ui.ActionBar("center", [
    ui.Button("primary", "New round", "c_start", 0, true)
  ])),
  ui.When(state.c_message !== "", ui.Text("caption", state.c_message))
]));
sections.push(ui.Section("content", "Guesses", "", [
  ui.When(state.c_guesses.length() === 0, ui.EmptyState("default", "No guesses yet", "Type a five-letter word and submit it.", "", "", "list")),
  ui.When(state.c_guesses.length() > 0, ui.Column("default", c_rows))
]));

metadata.label: word-games-04
needs: A hidden five-letter word chosen by the app at the start of each round, kept secret until the round ends. The person types a five-letter guess and taps to submit it; the phone marks each letter of the guess as correct in the right place, present but in the wrong place, or absent, and shows the guesses so far with their marks. After five wrong guesses the round ends and the hidden word is revealed; a correct guess ends the round early. A button starts a new round with a fresh hidden word.
letter-by-letter feedback marks

messages.content: You write the bodies of small functions for a program in the Vera language, which reads like TypeScript. Reply with strict JSON and nothing else: {"holes": {"<key>": "<body>"}}. Each body is only the statements inside the function braces, ending in a return of the declared type: no function header, no braces around it, no comments, no markdown. Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.

Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.

function c_weekdayOf(state: AppState, index: number): number {
  let e: LogEntry = state.entries[index];
  let day: number = time.daysSinceEpoch();
  let back: number = 0;
  let i: number = state.entries.length() - 1;
  while (i > index) {
    back = back + 1;
    i = i - 1;
  }
  let d: number = day - back;
  let w: number = (d + 4) % 7;
  if (w < 0) { w = w + 7; }
  return w;
}

function c_weekdayTotal(state: AppState, weekday: number): number {
  let total: number = 0;
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < state.entries.length()) {
    if (c_weekdayOf(state, i) === weekday) {
      total = total + state.entries[i].glasses;
    }
    i = i + 1;
  }
  return total;
}

function c_weekdayCount(state: AppState, weekday: number): number {
  let count: number = 0;
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < state.entries.length()) {
    if (c_weekdayOf(state, i) === weekday) {
      count = count + 1;
    }
    i = i + 1;
  }
  return count;
}

function c_weekdayAverage(state: AppState, weekday: number): number {
  let count: number = c_weekdayCount(state, weekday);
  if (count === 0) { return 0; }
  return c_weekdayTotal(state, weekday) / count;
}

function c_weekdayName(weekday: number): string {
  if (weekday === 0) { return "Sun"; }
  if (weekday === 1) { return "Mon"; }
  if (weekday === 2) { return "Tue"; }
  if (weekday === 3) { return "Wed"; }
  if (weekday === 4) { return "Thu"; }
  if (weekday === 5) { return "Fri"; }
  return "Sat";
}

    c_body.push(ui.Text("muted", "Your weekday averages appear once you log your first glass."));

    let c_order: number[] = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 0];

- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.

Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.

<classes>

</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. function c_dayIndex(name: string): number {

Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:

Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.
- A function that opens another app with the action ready for the person to confirm (a message filled in, a contact form, a route) does the job: use it, and say on the screen that the person confirms it there.
- Before answering <cannot>, go through the phone functions found for each need: when one does it -- even by parts, such as audio samples written to a renderer, or the flashlight switched on and off -- write the section with it.
- A need worded as something to do inside this app that the app cannot do (it has no such component) is not refused if a function found does the nearest useful thing for the person -- shows or opens the same thing in the app made for it: write the section with that function, and say in a line on the screen what it does instead.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them, as said below.
- If none of the phone functions found does what is needed, or it needs something the phone cannot give a program (a camera, a live feed, the person's location), decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.

Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.

messages.content:
Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.
- A function that opens another app with the action ready for the person to confirm (a message filled in, a contact form, a route) does the job: use it, and say on the screen that the person confirms it there.
- Before answering <cannot>, go through the phone functions found for each need: when one does it -- even by parts, such as audio samples written to a renderer, or the flashlight switched on and off -- write the section with it.
- A need worded as something to do inside this app that the app cannot do (it has no such component) is not refused if a function found does the nearest useful thing for the person -- shows or opens the same thing in the app made for it: write the section with that function, and say in a line on the screen what it does instead.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them, as said below.
- If none of the phone functions found does what is needed, or it needs something the phone cannot give a program (a camera, a live feed, the person's location), decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.
- Suggestions, ideas, recipes, tips or questions made FROM WHAT THE PERSON ENTERED (dinners from the items in their pantry, questions from their notes, a plan from the times they set) are written by the model while the app runs, never by the section: a fixed sentence with their words pasted in ("Roast vegetable tray, uses Spinach") is not a suggestion. The section has a button that asks, a "pending" text while it waits, and the answer shown as text:
    function suggest(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
      sdk.call("Vera.Ask.text", ["prompt", "Two quick dinners using: " + names + ". One line each.", "maxWords", "60"], "onSuggested");
      return {c_ideas: "Thinking..."__PASSTHROUGH__};
    }
    function onSuggested(state: AppState, value: string): AppState { return {c_ideas: value__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  An answer starting with "error" is shown as a failure the person can try again. Call it only from a button's handler, never from view() or a ticker; and never for numbers the app works out itself or for anything known when the app is made.

function c_pick(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let n: number = state.ideas7.length();
  if (n === 0) { return {__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  let pool: number[] = [];
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < n) {
    let used: boolean = false;
    for (let u: number of state.c_used) { if (u === i) { used = true; } }
    if (!used) { pool.push(i); }
    i = i + 1;
  }
  if (pool.length() === 0) { return {__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  let seed: number = state.c_seed + 1;
  let pick: number = pool[math.randomBelow(seed, pool.length())];
  let out: number[] = [];
  for (let u2: number of state.c_used) { out.push(u2); }
  out.push(pick);
  return {c_used: out, c_tonight: pick, c_seed: seed__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_reset(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let empty: number[] = [];
  return {c_used: empty, c_tonight: -1__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_setTitle(state: AppState, value: string): AppState {
  return {c_newTitle: value__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_setMinutes(state: AppState, value: string): AppState {
  return {c_newMinutes: value__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_addRecipe(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let title: string = strings.trim(state.c_newTitle);
  let mins: number = strings.toNumber(strings.trim(state.c_newMinutes), -1);
  if (title.length() === 0 || mins <= 0) {
    return {c_addTried: true__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  let out: Idea[] = [];
  for (let it: Idea of state.ideas7) { out.push(it); }
  out.push({title: title, minutes: math.round(mins), level: "", how: "", doneDay: -1});
  return {ideas7: out, c_newTitle: "", c_newMinutes: "", c_addTried: false__PASSTHROUGH__};
}
</functions>
<view>
{
  let n: number = state.ideas7.length();
  let left: number = n - state.c_used.length();
  if (left < 0) { left = 0; }
  let body: ui.View[] = [];
  if (state.c_tonight >= 0 && state.c_tonight < n) {
    let it: Idea = state.ideas7[state.c_tonight];
    let meta: string = ui.numberToString(it.minutes) + " min";
    if (it.level.length() > 0) { meta = meta + " · " + it.level; }
    body.push(ui.Text("caption", "Tonight's dinner"));
    body.push(ui.Text("title", it.title));
    body.push(ui.Text("muted", meta));
    if (it.how.length() > 0) { body.push(ui.Text("body", it.how)); }
  } else {
    body.push(ui.Text("muted", "Tap Pick tonight and the phone chooses a recipe you have not used yet."));
  }
  let actions: ui.View[] = [];
  if (left > 0) {
    actions.push(ui.Button("primary", "Pick tonight", "c_pick", 0, true));
  }
  if (state.c_used.length() > 0) {
    actions.push(ui.Button("secondary", "Start over", "c_reset", 0, true));
  }
  if (actions.length() > 0) { body.push(ui.ActionBar("end", actions)); }
  if (left === 0 && n > 0) {
    body.push(ui.Text("muted", "Every recipe has been used, so there is nothing left to pick."));
  }
  sections.push(ui.Section("content", "Tonight's pick", ui.numberToString(left) + " of " + ui.numberToString(n) + " still unused", body));

  let addBody: ui.View[] = [];
  addBody.push(ui.TextField("default", "Recipe title", state.c_newTitle, "c_setTitle"));
  addBody.push(ui.TextField("default", "Minutes", state.c_newMinutes, "c_setMinutes", "number"));
  if (state.c_addTried) {
    addBody.push(ui.Text("warning", "Enter a title and a number of minutes greater than zero."));
  }
  addBody.push(ui.ActionBar("end", [
    ui.Button("primary", "Add recipe", "c_addRecipe", 0, true)
  ]));
  sections.push(ui.Section("content", "Add your own recipe", "It joins the pool for tonight's pick", addBody));
}

messages.content:
Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};

</fields>
<functions>
function c_makeShelf(): C_Book[] {
  let out: C_Book[] = [];
  out.push({title: "Pride and Prejudice", author: "Jane Austen", read: false});
  out.push({title: "The Hobbit", author: "J. R. R. Tolkien", read: false});
  out.push({title: "Dune", author: "Frank Herbert", read: false});
  out.push({title: "To Kill a Mockingbird", author: "Harper Lee", read: false});
  out.push({title: "1984", author: "George Orwell", read: false});
  out.push({title: "The Great Gatsby", author: "F. Scott Fitzgerald", read: false});
  out.push({title: "Moby-Dick", author: "Herman Melville", read: false});
  out.push({title: "Jane Eyre", author: "Charlotte Bronte", read: false});
  out.push({title: "The Catcher in the Rye", author: "J. D. Salinger", read: false});
  out.push({title: "Frankenstein", author: "Mary Shelley", read: false});
  out.push({title: "The Odyssey", author: "Homer", read: false});
  out.push({title: "Beloved", author: "Toni Morrison", read: false});
  return out;
}

function c_ensure(state: AppState): C_Book[] {
  if (state.c_shelf.length() === 0) {
    return c_makeShelf();
  }
  return state.c_shelf;
}

function c_pick(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let shelf: C_Book[] = c_ensure(state);
  let unread: number = 0;
  for (let b: C_Book of shelf) {
    if (!b.read) { unread = unread + 1; }
  }
  let want: number = state.pickCount;
  if (want > unread) { want = unread; }
  let seed: number = state.c_seed;
  let chosen: string[] = [];
  let next: C_Book[] = [];
  for (let b: C_Book of shelf) {
    next.push({title: b.title, author: b.author, read: b.read});
  }
  let taken: number = 0;
  while (taken < want) {
    let pool: number = 0;
    for (let b: C_Book of next) {
      if (!b.read) { pool = pool + 1; }
    }
    if (pool === 0) { taken = want; } else {
      let r: number = math.randomBelow(seed, pool);
      seed = math.randomStep(seed);
      let idx: number = 0;
      let seen: number = 0;
      let i: number = 0;
      while (i < next.length()) {
        let b: C_Book = next[i];
        if (!b.read) {
          if (seen === r) { idx = i; }
          seen = seen + 1;
        }
        i = i + 1;
      }
      let pick: C_Book = next[idx];
      chosen.push(pick.title);
      next[idx] = {title: pick.title, author: pick.author, read: true};
      taken = taken + 1;
    }
  }
  return {c_shelf: next, c_current: chosen, c_seed: seed, c_picked: true__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_reset(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let empty: string[] = [];
  return {c_shelf: c_makeShelf(), c_current: empty, c_picked: false__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_setNewTitle(state: AppState, value: string): AppState {
  return {c_newTitle: value__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_setNewAuthor(state: AppState, value: string): AppState {
  return {c_newAuthor: value__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_addBook(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let title: string = strings.trim(state.c_newTitle);
  if (title === "") {
    return {c_addTried: true__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  let shelf: C_Book[] = c_ensure(state);
  let out: C_Book[] = [];
  for (let b: C_Book of shelf) {
    out.push({title: b.title, author: b.author, read: b.read});
  }
  out.push({title: title, author: strings.trim(state.c_newAuthor), read: false});
  return {c_shelf: out, c_newTitle: "", c_newAuthor: "", c_addTried: false__PASSTHROUGH__};
}
</functions>
<view>
{
  let shelf: C_Book[] = c_ensure(state);
  let unread: number = 0;
  let readCount: number = 0;
  for (let b: C_Book of shelf) {
    if (b.read) { readCount = readCount + 1; } else { unread = unread + 1; }
  }
  let currentRows: ui.View[] = [];
  for (let t: string of state.c_current) {
    let author: string = "";
    for (let b: C_Book of shelf) {
      if (b.title === t) { author = b.author; }
    }
    currentRows.push(ui.ListItem("accent", t, author, "", "", 0, true, "check"));
  }
  let shelfRows: ui.View[] = [];
  for (let b: C_Book of shelf) {
    let trailing: string = "Unread";
    if (b.read) { trailing = "Read"; }
    shelfRows.push(ui.ListItem("default", b.title, b.author, trailing, "", 0, true, ""));
  }
  let pickLabel: string = "Pick " + ui.numberToString(state.pickCount) + " book";
  if (state.pickCount !== 1) { pickLabel = pickLabel + "s"; }
  sections.push(ui.Section("content", "Pick", ui.numberToString(unread) + " unread of " + ui.numberToString(shelf.length()), [
    ui.ActionBar("end", [
      ui.Button("primary", pickLabel, "c_pick", 0, unread > 0),
      ui.Button("secondary", "Reset shelf", "c_reset", 0, readCount > 0)
    ]),
    ui.When(state.c_picked && state.c_current.length() === 0,
      ui.InsetBanner("warning", "Shelf finished", "Every book has been read. Reset the shelf to start over.", "", "", "info")),
    ui.When(state.c_current.length() > 0, ui.ListGroup("default", "Current pick", currentRows))
  ]));
  sections.push(ui.Section("content", "Add a book", "", [
    ui.TextField("default", "Title", state.c_newTitle, "c_setNewTitle"),
    ui.TextField("default", "Author", state.c_newAuthor, "c_setNewAuthor"),
    ui.When(state.c_addTried && strings.trim(state.c_newTitle) === "",
      ui.Text("caption", "Enter a book title first.")),
    ui.ActionBar("end", [
      ui.Button("primary", "Add to shelf", "c_addBook", 0, true)
    ])
  ]));
  sections.push(ui.Section("content", "Shelf", "", [
    ui.ListGroup("default", "", shelfRows)
  ]));
}
</view>

messages.content:
Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.
- A function that opens another app with the action ready for the person to confirm (a message filled in, a contact form, a route) does the job: use it, and say on the screen that the person confirms it there.
- Before answering <cannot>, go through the phone functions found for each need: when one does it -- even by parts, such as audio samples written to a renderer, or the flashlight switched on and off -- write the section with it.
- A need worded as something to do inside this app that the app cannot do (it has no such component) is not refused if a function found does the nearest useful thing for the person -- shows or opens the same thing in the app made for it: write the section with that function, and say in a line on the screen what it does instead.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them, as said below.
- If none of the phone functions found does what is needed, or it needs something the phone cannot give a program (a camera, a live feed, the person's location), decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.
- Suggestions, ideas, recipes, tips or questions made FROM WHAT THE PERSON ENTERED (dinners from the items in their pantry, questions from their notes, a plan from the times they set) are written by the model while the app runs, never by the section: a fixed sentence with their words pasted in ("Roast vegetable tray, uses Spinach") is not a suggestion. function c_diff(a: string, b: string): number {
  if (strings.length(a) !== 4 || strings.length(b) !== 4) { return -1; }
  let n: number = 0;
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < 4) {
    if (strings.substring(a, i, i + 1) !== strings.substring(b, i, i + 1)) { n = n + 1; }
    i = i + 1;
  }
  return n;
}

function c_latest(state: AppState): string {
  let n: number = state.entries.length();
  if (n === 0) { return ""; }
  return state.entries[n - 1].word;
}

function c_lettersChanged(state: AppState): number {
  let latest: string = c_latest(state);
  if (latest === "") { return 0; }
  let d: number = c_diff(state.startWord, latest);
  if (d < 0) { return 0; }
  return d;
}

function c_solved(state: AppState): number {
  let latest: string = c_latest(state);
  if (latest === "" || state.endWord === "") { return 0; }
  if (strings.toLowerCase(latest) === strings.toLowerCase(state.endWord)) { return 1; }
  return 0;
}

function c_rungWarning(state: AppState): string {
  let n: number = state.entries.length();
  if (n === 0) { return ""; }
  let latest: string = strings.toLowerCase(state.entries[n - 1].word);
  let previous: string = "";
  if (n >= 2) {
    previous = strings.toLowerCase(state.entries[n - 2].word);
  } else {
    previous = strings.toLowerCase(state.startWord);
  }
  if (strings.length(previous) !== 4) {
    return "Set a four-letter start word so the first rung can be checked.";
  }
  if (strings.length(latest) !== 4) {
    return "The rung \"" + state.entries[n - 1].word + "\" is not four letters long.";
  }
  let d: number = c_diff(previous, latest);
  if (d === 0) {
    return "The rung \"" + state.entries[n - 1].word + "\" is the same as \"" + previous + "\" — change exactly one letter.";
  }
  if (d !== 1) {
    return "The rung \"" + state.entries[n - 1].word + "\" is " + ui.numberToString(d) + " letters away from \"" + previous + "\" — change exactly one letter.";
  }
  return "";
}

messages.content:
Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.

function c_diff(a: string, b: string): number {

  return d;
}

function c_diff(a: string, b: string): number {
  if (strings.length(a) !== 4 || strings.length(b) !== 4) { return -1; }
  let n: number = 0;
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < 4) {
    if (strings.substring(a, i, i + 1) !== strings.substring(b, i, i + 1)) { n = n + 1; }
    i = i + 1;
  }
  return n;
}

function c_latest(state: AppState): string {
  let n: number = state.entries.length();
  if (n === 0) { return ""; }
  return state.entries[n - 1].word;
}

function c_lettersChanged(state: AppState): number {
  let latest: string = c_latest(state);
  if (latest === "") { return 0; }
  let d: number = c_diff(state.startWord, latest);
  if (d < 0) { return 0; }
  return d;
}

function c_solved(state: AppState): number {
  let latest: string = c_latest(state);
  if (latest === "" || state.endWord === "") { return 0; }
  if (strings.toLowerCase(latest) === strings.toLowerCase(state.endWord)) { return 1; }
  return 0;
}

function c_resetRungs(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let none: LogEntry[] = [];
  return {entries: none, removedEntries: none, removedAt: -1, draft_word: ""__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

messages.content:
Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.
- A function that opens another app with the action ready for the person to confirm (a message filled in, a contact form, a route) does the job: use it, and say on the screen that the person confirms it there.
- Before answering <cannot>, go through the phone functions found for each need: when one does it -- even by parts, such as audio samples written to a renderer, or the flashlight switched on and off -- write the section with it.
- A need worded as something to do inside this app that the app cannot do (it has no such component) is not refused if a function found does the nearest useful thing for the person -- shows or opens the same thing in the app made for it: write the section with that function, and say in a line on the screen what it does instead.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them, as said below.
- If none of the phone functions found does what is needed, or it needs something the phone cannot give a program (a camera, a live feed, the person's location), decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.
- Suggestions, ideas, recipes, tips or questions made FROM WHAT THE PERSON ENTERED (dinners from the items in their pantry, questions from their notes, a plan from the times they set) are written by the model while the app runs, never by the section: a fixed sentence with their words pasted in ("Roast vegetable tray, uses Spinach") is not a suggestion. The section has a button that asks, a "pending" text while it waits, and the answer shown as text:
    function suggest(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
      sdk.call("Vera.Ask.text", ["prompt", "Two quick dinners using: " + names + ". One line each.", "maxWords", "60"], "onSuggested");
      return {c_ideas: "Thinking..."__PASSTHROUGH__};
    }
    function onSuggested(state: AppState, value: string): AppState { return {c_ideas: value__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  An answer starting with "error" is shown as a failure the person can try again. Call it only from a button's handler, never from view() or a ticker; and never for numbers the app works out itself or for anything known when the app is made.

Request: word ladder game with four letter words

The section must do:
- A built-in list of common four-letter English words the app checks each rung against, so every word typed must be four letters and one letter different from the word before it; the person reads the rules and the example ladder shown at the start.
- the figure "Letters changed": how many letters differ between the start word and the latest rung, counting each position once (the plan works it out as entryCount; for entryCount = 5 that is 5)
- the figure "Solved": whether the latest rung matches the end word (a yes or a no worked out as 1 or 0: show it as Yes or No, or as words that say which, never as the number) (the plan works it out as 0; for its example that is 0)

The person sets these on the screen and nothing else uses them yet; the section uses them:
- "Start word": state.startWord
- "End word": state.endWord

The program already has these: use them, do not make your own:
- a list of entries: state.entries is LogEntry[] with the fields {word: string, minute: number}. Its form, its Add and Remove buttons and its rows are already on the screen. The section makes no list of its own for the same entries; to add one it copies state.entries into a new array, pushes a LogEntry (minute: time.hourOfDay() * 60 + time.minuteOfHour()) and returns {entries: thatArray __PASSTHROUGH__}.

Nothing they show is shown again: no second list, total, chart, Remove last or Start over button. While what the section works from is still empty, it shows one plain line saying what will appear and when, never a ui.EmptyState: the list above already has one (two empty states one under the other read as a broken screen).

function c_hintWord(letters: string, n: number, found: string): string {
  let dict: string[] = c_dictionary();
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < dict.length()) {
    let w: string = dict[i];
    if (strings.length(w) >= c_minWord() && !strings.contains(found, "|" + w + "|")) {
      if (c_wordInGrid(letters, n, w)) { return w; }
    }
    i = i + 1;
  }
  return "";
}

function c_wordInGrid(letters: string, n: number, word: string): boolean {
  let start: number = 0;
  while (start < n * n) {
    if (c_letterAt(letters, start) === strings.substring(word, 0, 1)) {
      let path: number[] = [];
      path.push(start);
      if (c_search(letters, n, word, path, 1)) { return true; }
    }
    start = start + 1;
  }
  return false;
}

function c_search(letters: string, n: number, word: string, path: number[], depth: number): boolean {
  if (depth >= strings.length(word)) { return true; }
  let last: number = path[path.length() - 1];
  let next: number = 0;
  while (next < n * n) {
    if (!c_inPath(path, next) && c_adjacent(last, next, n)) {
      if (c_letterAt(letters, next) === strings.substring(word, depth, depth + 1)) {
        let grown: number[] = [];
        let i: number = 0;
        while (i < path.length()) {
          grown.push(path[i]);
          i = i + 1;
        }
        grown.push(next);
        if (c_search(letters, n, word, grown, depth + 1)) { return true; }
      }
    }
    next = next + 1;
  }
  return false;
}

function c_hintPath(letters: string, n: number, word: string): number[] {
  let start: number = 0;
  while (start < n * n) {
    if (c_letterAt(letters, start) === strings.substring(word, 0, 1)) {
      let path: number[] = [];
      path.push(start);
      let found: number[] = c_searchPath(letters, n, word, path, 1);
      if (found.length() > 0) { return found; }
    }
    start = start + 1;
  }
  let empty: number[] = [];
  return empty;
}

function c_searchPath(letters: string, n: number, word: string, path: number[], depth: number): number[] {
  if (depth >= strings.length(word)) { return path; }
  let last: number = path[path.length() - 1];
  let next: number = 0;
  while (next < n * n) {
    if (!c_inPath(path, next) && c_adjacent(last, next, n)) {
      if (c_letterAt(letters, next) === strings.substring(word, depth, depth + 1)) {
        let grown: number[] = [];

messages.content:
Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.
- A function that opens another app with the action ready for the person to confirm (a message filled in, a contact form, a route) does the job: use it, and say on the screen that the person confirms it there.
- Before answering <cannot>, go through the phone functions found for each need: when one does it -- even by parts, such as audio samples written to a renderer, or the flashlight switched on and off -- write the section with it.
- A need worded as something to do inside this app that the app cannot do (it has no such component) is not refused if a function found does the nearest useful thing for the person -- shows or opens the same thing in the app made for it: write the section with that function, and say in a line on the screen what it does instead.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them, as said below.
- If none of the phone functions found does what is needed, or it needs something the phone cannot give a program (a camera, a live feed, the person's location), decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.
- Suggestions, ideas, recipes, tips or questions made FROM WHAT THE PERSON ENTERED (dinners from the items in their pantry, questions from their notes, a plan from the times they set) are written by the model while the app runs, never by the section: a fixed sentence with their words pasted in ("Roast vegetable tray, uses Spinach") is not a suggestion. The section has a button that asks, a "pending" text while it waits, and the answer shown as text:
    function suggest(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
      sdk.call("Vera.Ask.text", ["prompt", "Two quick dinners using: " + names + ". One line each.", "maxWords", "60"], "onSuggested");
      return {c_ideas: "Thinking..."__PASSTHROUGH__};
    }
    function onSuggested(state: AppState, value: string): AppState { return {c_ideas: value__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  An answer starting with "error" is shown as a failure the person can try again. Call it only from a button's handler, never from view() or a ticker; and never for numbers the app works out itself or for anything known when the app is made.

function c_buildPuzzles(): C_Puzzle[] {
  let out: C_Puzzle[] = [];
  out.push({emoji: "🦁👑🌅", title: "The Lion King"});
  out.push({emoji: "🚢🧊💔", title: "Titanic"});

  out.push({emoji: "🐟🔍🌊", title: "Finding Nemo"});
  out.push({emoji: "🧙‍♂️💍🌋", title: "The Lord of the Rings"});
  out.push({emoji: "🚀🌌⭐", title: "Star Wars"});
  out.push({emoji: "🦖🏝️🧬", title: "Jurassic Park"});
  out.push({emoji: "👽📞🏠", title: "E.T."});
  out.push({emoji: "🐻🍯🌳", title: "Winnie the Pooh"});
  out.push({emoji: "🎩🐰🕳️", title: "Alice in Wonderland"});
  out.push({emoji: "🦇🧛🌃", title: "Batman"});
  out.push({emoji: "🐼🥋🌿", title: "Kung Fu Panda"});
  out.push({emoji: "🚗💨🏁", title: "Fast & Furious"});
  out.push({emoji: "🧜‍♀️🌊👑", title: "The Little Mermaid"});
  return out;
}

function c_shuffle(state: AppState, count: number): AppState {
  let puzzles: C_Puzzle[] = c_buildPuzzles();
  let n: number = puzzles.length();
  let order: number[] = [];
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < n) {
    order.push(i);
    i = i + 1;
  }
  let seed: number = state.c_seed;
  let j: number = n - 1;
  while (j > 0) {
    seed = math.randomStep(seed);
    let k: number = math.randomBelow(seed, j + 1);
    let tmp: number = order[j];
    order[j] = order[k];
    order[k] = tmp;
    j = j - 1;
  }
  return {c_puzzles: puzzles, c_order: order, c_round: 0, c_guess: "", c_revealed: false, c_correct: false, c_started: true, c_seed: seed, c_hint: false__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_start(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  return c_shuffle(state, state.roundsPerGame);
}

function c_setGuess(state: AppState, value: string): AppState {
  return {c_guess: value__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_showHint(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  return {c_hint: true__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_check(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  if (state.c_revealed) { return state; }
  if (state.c_order.length() === 0) { return state; }
  if (state.c_round >= state.c_order.length()) { return state; }
  let idx: number = state.c_order[state.c_round];
  let answer: string = state.c_puzzles[idx].title;
  let ok: boolean = strings.toLowerCase(strings.trim(state.c_guess)) === strings.toLowerCase(answer);
  let out: LogEntry[] = [];
  for (let e: LogEntry of state.entries) { out.push(e); }
  out.push({guess: strings.trim(state.c_guess), minute: time.hourOfDay() * 60 + time.minuteOfHour()});
  return {c_revealed: true, c_correct: ok, entries: out__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_next(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  if (!state.c_revealed) { return state; }
  return {c_round: state.c_round + 1, c_guess: "", c_revealed: false, c_correct: false, c_hint: false__PASSTHROUGH__};
}
</functions>
<view>
{
  let total: number = state.c_order.length();
  let done: boolean = state.c_started && total > 0 && state.c_round >= total;
  let children: ui.View[] = [];
  if (!state.c_started) {
    children.push(ui.Text("body", "Tap Start to shuffle " + ui.numberToString(state.roundsPerGame) + " emoji puzzles."));
    children.push(ui.ActionBar("end", [ui.Button("primary", "Start quiz", "c_start", 0, true)]));
  } else if (done) {
    children.push(ui.Text("heading", "All " + ui.numberToString(total) + " puzzles done."));
    children.push(ui.ActionBar("end", [ui.Button("primary", "Play again", "c_start", 0, true)]));
  } else {
    let idx: number = state.c_order[state.c_round];
    let puzzle: C_Puzzle = state.c_puzzles[idx];
    children.push(ui.Text("caption", "Puzzle " + ui.numberToString(state.c_round + 1) + " of " + ui.numberToString(total)));
    children.push(ui.Text("display", puzzle.emoji));
    if (!state.c_revealed) {
      if (state.c_hint) {
        let first: string = strings.substring(puzzle.title, 0, 1);
        children.push(ui.InsetBanner("accent", "Hint", "The answer starts with \"" + first + "\"", "", "", "info"));
      }
      children.push(ui.TextField("default", "Your guess", state.c_guess, "c_setGuess"));
      children.push(ui.ActionBar("end", [
        ui.Button("secondary", "Hint", "c_showHint", 0, !state.c_hint),
        ui.Button("primary", "Check", "c_check", 0, strings.trim(state.c_guess) !== "")
      ]));
    } else {
      if (state.c_correct) {
        children.push(ui.InsetBanner("success", "Correct!", puzzle.title, "", "", "check"));
      } else {
        children.push(ui.InsetBanner("danger", "Not quite", "The answer was " + puzzle.title, "", "", "close"));
      }
      children.push(ui.ActionBar("end", [ui.Button("primary", "Next puzzle", "c_next", 0, true)]));
    }
  }
  sections.push(ui.Section("content", "Emoji clues", "", children));
}
