Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.
- A function that opens another app with the action ready for the person to confirm (a message filled in, a contact form, a route) does the job: use it, and say on the screen that the person confirms it there.
- Before answering <cannot>, go through the phone functions found for each need: when one does it -- even by parts, such as audio samples written to a renderer, or the flashlight switched on and off -- write the section with it.
- A need worded as something to do inside this app that the app cannot do (it has no such component) is not refused if a function found does the nearest useful thing for the person -- shows or opens the same thing in the app made for it: write the section with that function, and say in a line on the screen what it does instead.
- Words written from what the person entered (suggestions, recipes, ideas) are never declined: "Vera.Ask.text" writes them, as said below.
- If none of the phone functions found does what is needed, or it needs something the phone cannot give a program (a camera, a live feed, the person's location), decline that need as above, beside the rest; a bare <cannot>one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.
- Suggestions, ideas, recipes, tips or questions made FROM WHAT THE PERSON ENTERED (dinners from the items in their pantry, questions from their notes, a plan from the times they set) are written by the model while the app runs, never by the section: a fixed sentence with their words pasted in ("Roast vegetable tray, uses Spinach") is not a suggestion. The section has a button that asks, a "pending" text while it waits, and the answer shown as text:
    function suggest(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
      sdk.call("Vera.Ask.text", ["prompt", "Two quick dinners using: " + names + ". One line each.", "maxWords", "60"], "onSuggested");
      return {c_ideas: "Thinking..."__PASSTHROUGH__};
    }
    function onSuggested(state: AppState, value: string): AppState { return {c_ideas: value__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
  An answer starting with "error" is shown as a failure the person can try again. Call it only from a button's handler, never from view() or a ticker; and never for numbers the app works out itself or for anything known when the app is made.

</fields>
<functions>
function c_buildPuzzles(): C_Puzzle[] {
  let out: C_Puzzle[] = [];
  out.push({emoji: "🦁👑🌅", title: "The Lion King"});
  out.push({emoji: "🚢🧊💔", title: "Titanic"});
  out.push({emoji: "🕷️🕸️🦸", title: "Spider-Man"});
  out.push({emoji: "🦈🌊😱", title: "Jaws"});
  out.push({emoji: "👻🚫👨", title: "Ghostbusters"});
  out.push({emoji: "🐟🔍🌊", title: "Finding Nemo"});
  out.push({emoji: "🧙‍♂️💍🌋", title: "The Lord of the Rings"});
  out.push({emoji: "🚀🌌⭐", title: "Star Wars"});
  out.push({emoji: "🦖🏝️🧬", title: "Jurassic Park"});
  out.push({emoji: "👽📞🏠", title: "E.T."});
  out.push({emoji: "🐻🍯🌳", title: "Winnie the Pooh"});
  out.push({emoji: "🎩🐰🕳️", title: "Alice in Wonderland"});
  out.push({emoji: "🦇🧛🌃", title: "Batman"});
  out.push({emoji: "🐼🥋🌿", title: "Kung Fu Panda"});
  out.push({emoji: "🚗💨🏁", title: "Fast & Furious"});
  out.push({emoji: "🧜‍♀️🌊👑", title: "The Little Mermaid"});
  return out;
}

function c_shuffle(state: AppState, count: number): AppState {
  let puzzles: C_Puzzle[] = c_buildPuzzles();
  let n: number = puzzles.length();
  let order: number[] = [];
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < n) {
    order.push(i);
    i = i + 1;
  }
  let seed: number = state.c_seed;
  let j: number = n - 1;
  while (j > 0) {
    seed = math.randomStep(seed);
    let k: number = math.randomBelow(seed, j + 1);
    let tmp: number = order[j];
    order[j] = order[k];
    order[k] = tmp;
    j = j - 1;
  }
  return {c_puzzles: puzzles, c_order: order, c_round: 0, c_guess: "", c_revealed: false, c_correct: false, c_started: true, c_seed: seed, c_seconds: 0, c_running: true__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_start(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  return c_shuffle(state, state.roundsPerGame);
}

function c_setGuess(state: AppState, value: string): AppState {
  return {c_guess: value__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_check(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  if (state.c_revealed) { return state; }
  if (state.c_order.length() === 0) { return state; }
  if (state.c_round >= state.c_order.length()) { return state; }
  let idx: number = state.c_order[state.c_round];
  let answer: string = state.c_puzzles[idx].title;
  let ok: boolean = strings.toLowerCase(strings.trim(state.c_guess)) === strings.toLowerCase(answer);
  let out: LogEntry[] = [];
  for (let e: LogEntry of state.entries) { out.push(e); }
  out.push({guess: strings.trim(state.c_guess), minute: time.hourOfDay() * 60 + time.minuteOfHour()});
  return {c_revealed: true, c_correct: ok, c_running: false, entries: out__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_next(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  if (!state.c_revealed) { return state; }
  return {c_round: state.c_round + 1, c_guess: "", c_revealed: false, c_correct: false, c_seconds: 0, c_running: true__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_tick(state: AppState, elapsedMs: number): AppState {
  if (!state.c_running) { return state; }
  let add: number = math.floor(elapsedMs / 1000);
  if (add < 1) { return state; }
  return {c_seconds: state.c_seconds + add__PASSTHROUGH__};
}
</functions>
<view>
{
  let total: number = state.c_order.length();
  let done: boolean = state.c_started && total > 0 && state.c_round >= total;
  let children: ui.View[] = [];
  if (!state.c_started) {
    children.push(ui.Text("body", "Tap Start to shuffle " + ui.numberToString(state.roundsPerGame) + " emoji puzzles."));
    children.push(ui.ActionBar("end", [ui.Button("primary", "Start quiz", "c_start", 0, true)]));
  } else if (done) {
    children.push(ui.Text("heading", "All " + ui.numberToString(total) + " puzzles done."));
    children.push(ui.ActionBar("end", [ui.Button("primary", "Play again", "c_start", 0, true)]));
  } else {
    let idx: number = state.c_order[state.c_round];
    let puzzle: C_Puzzle = state.c_puzzles[idx];
    children.push(ui.Text("caption", "Puzzle " + ui.numberToString(state.c_round + 1) + " of " + ui.numberToString(total)));
    children.push(ui.Text("display", puzzle.emoji));
    children.push(ui.Text("metric", ui.durationToString(state.c_seconds)));
    children.push(ui.Ticker("default", "c_puzzleClock", 1000, state.c_running, "c_tick"));
    if (!state.c_revealed) {
      children.push(ui.TextField("default", "Your guess", state.c_guess, "c_setGuess"));
      children.push(ui.ActionBar("end", [ui.Button("primary", "Check", "c_check", 0, strings.trim(state.c_guess) !== "")]));
    } else {
      if (state.c_correct) {
        children.push(ui.InsetBanner("success", "Correct!", puzzle.title, "", "", "check"));
      } else {
        children.push(ui.InsetBanner("danger", "Not quite", "The answer was " + puzzle.title, "", "", "close"));
      }
      children.push(ui.ActionBar("end", [ui.Button("primary", "Next puzzle", "c_next", 0, true)]));
    }
  }
  sections.push(ui.Section("content", "Emoji clues", "", children));
}

function c_shuffleLettersInPlace(letters: string, seed: number): string {
  let chars: string[] = [];
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < letters.length()) {
    chars.push(strings.substring(letters, i, i + 1));
    i = i + 1;
  }
  let s: number = seed;
  let n: number = chars.length();
  let j: number = n - 1;
  while (j > 0) {
    s = math.randomStep(s);
    let k: number = math.randomBelow(s, j + 1);
    let tmp: string = chars[j];
    chars[j] = chars[k];
    chars[k] = tmp;
    j = j - 1;
  }
  let out: string = "";
  for (let ch: string of chars) {
    out = out + ch;
  }
  return out;
}

function c_shuffle(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let seed: number = math.randomStep(state.c_shuffleSeed);
  let letters: string = c_shuffleLettersInPlace(state.c_letters, seed);
  return {c_letters: letters, c_shuffleSeed: seed, elapsedMs: state.elapsedMs, running: state.running, finished: state.finished, roundLengthIndex: state.roundLengthIndex, c_letterSeed: state.c_letterSeed, c_input: state.c_input, c_words: state.c_words, c_lengths: state.c_lengths, c_message: state.c_message, c_tried: state.c_tried, c_round: state.c_round, c_checking: state.c_checking, c_checkWord: state.c_checkWord};
}

messages.content:
Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.
- When some of the needs cannot be done but others can, write the section for the ones that can and add, for each one that cannot, <cannot need="the need, copied exactly">one short sentence for the person using the app, in plain words about their phone and its apps: what this app cannot do, and why. Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.
- What the phone or another app must do, the section does with sdk.call from a handler, calling ONLY targets from "Phone functions found" in the request (and "Vera.Ask.text", as said below), copied exactly, with the parameters they show, values from the screen's state. Its answer handler shows what came back: an answer starting with "declined" or "error" is a failure, anything else succeeded.

Now you do not write a whole program. You add ONE section to a VERA-L program that already exists, and you write only that section, in exactly this form and nothing else:
<classes>
any @jsonable record classes the section needs, or nothing
</classes>
<fields>
one state field per line, as  name: type = initial value  (or nothing)
</fields>
<functions>
the handlers and helper functions the section needs
</functions>
<view>
statements that build the section and add it with sections.push(ui.Section(...));
</view>
Rules for the section:
- Begin the name of every class, field and function with c_ (classes with C_), so nothing clashes with the program.
- A handler returns only the fields it changes, followed by __PASSTHROUGH__ just before the closing brace, which stands for every other field of the state kept as it is: return {c_count: state.c_count + 1__PASSTHROUGH__};
- The view statements run inside view(state): they may read any state field, but the local variables of the program's other sections are not visible there.
- Do not repeat, change or restyle anything the program already has. Do what the section must do, completely.
- If the program already has a clock (Start, Stop, Reset buttons, a time shown) or a list of entries with its own Add button, the section draws no clock, no Start/Stop/Reset buttons and no second list of the same entries: it works with that state and shows only what is new.
- A message about an empty or wrong field (such as "Enter a task name") is shown only after the person has tried to add it, never while the field is still untouched.
- Show each piece of information once: no heading and caption that say the same thing, and no second view (a table, "splits") of entries the program already lists in rows. A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.
- A list the section keeps that starts empty has its own way to add to it, and to remove from it: an empty list nothing can fill is a dead end (Chore stars: "No rewards yet" with no way to add one).
- Every number the section shows is worked out from something on the screen or named in the request: progress toward a goal needs the goal, set on the screen or fixed by the request, not a percent of nothing.
- Never write a phone number, address or other real-world contact the request did not give: a made-up number (such as +1 800 555 0100) looks real to the person. Show a field for the person to fill in, or say to call their local emergency number.

Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> beside it. Answer a bare <cannot> only when none can be done.
- A need declined has no button or row that claims to do it. If the section offers the nearest thing instead (an event in the phone calendar for a notification it cannot send), its button says that thing ("Add to calendar"), and the <cannot> sentence says what is offered instead. A notice saying it cannot beside a button named for the same thing reads as broken.
- A need the section does in its own way is done, not declined: guidance written out as rows is the care card or tips card asked for, a list is a "card", a field the person fills in is a setting. <cannot need> is only for what the person does not get at all on this screen, never for how it looks.

- Before answering <cannot>, go through the phone functions found for each need: when one does it -- even by parts, such as audio samples written to a renderer, or the flashlight switched on and off -- write the section with it.
- A need worded as something to do inside this app that the app cannot do (it has no such component) is not refused if a function found does the nearest useful thing for the person -- shows or opens the same thing in the app made for it: write the section with that function, and say in a line on the screen what it does instead.

Never mention the language, the section, sdk.call or code</cannot> only when none of the needs can be done. Never fake it, never pretend a call happened, never call a target that is not listed.

The section has a button that asks, a "pending" text while it waits, and the answer shown as text:

<classes>
@jsonable
class C_Country {
  name: string;
  done: boolean;
  correct: boolean;
}
</classes>
<fields>
c_countries: C_Country[] = []
c_guess: string = ""
c_index: number = 0
c_attempted: boolean = false
c_feedback: string = ""
c_right: number = 0
c_wrong: number = 0
c_seed: number = 7
</fields>
<functions>
function c_makeList(seed: number): C_Country[] {
  let names: string[] = [];
  names.push("France");
  names.push("Brazil");
  names.push("Japan");
  names.push("Kenya");
  names.push("Canada");
  names.push("Norway");
  names.push("Mexico");
  names.push("India");
  let out: C_Country[] = [];
  let s: number = seed;
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < names.length()) {
    out.push({name: names[i], done: false, correct: false});
    i = i + 1;
  }
  let n: number = out.length();
  let j: number = n - 1;
  while (j > 0) {
    s = math.randomStep(s);
    let k: number = math.randomBelow(s, j + 1);
    let a: C_Country = out[j];
    let b: C_Country = out[k];
    out[j] = b;
    out[k] = a;
    j = j - 1;
  }
  return out;
}

function c_ensure(state: AppState): C_Country[] {
  if (state.c_countries.length() === 0) {
    return c_makeList(state.c_seed);
  }
  return state.c_countries;
}

function c_hint(name: string, letters: number): string {
  let n: number = letters;
  if (n < 1) { n = 1; }
  if (n > name.length()) { n = name.length(); }
  let out: string = "";
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < name.length()) {
    if (i < n) {
      out = out + strings.substring(name, i, i + 1);
    } else {
      out = out + "_";
    }
    i = i + 1;
  }
  return out;
}

function c_setGuess(state: AppState, value: string): AppState {
  return {c_guess: value__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_check(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let list: C_Country[] = c_ensure(state);
  let idx: number = state.c_index;
  if (idx >= list.length()) {
    return {c_countries: list, c_attempted: true, c_feedback: "All countries guessed. Start again to replay."__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  let typed: string = strings.trim(state.c_guess);
  if (typed.length() === 0) {
    return {c_countries: list, c_attempted: true, c_feedback: "Type a country name first."__PASSTHROUGH__};
  }
  let target: C_Country = list[idx];
  let ok: boolean = strings.toLowerCase(typed) === strings.toLowerCase(target.name);
  let out: C_Country[] = [];
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < list.length()) {
    let c: C_Country = list[i];
    if (i === idx) {
      out.push({name: c.name, done: true, correct: ok});
    } else {
      out.push({name: c.name, done: c.done, correct: c.correct});
    }
    i = i + 1;
  }
  let msg: string = "";
  if (ok) {
    msg = "Correct! It was " + target.name + ".";
  } else {
    msg = "Not quite. It was " + target.name + ".";
  }
  let right: number = state.c_right;
  let wrong: number = state.c_wrong;
  if (ok) { right = right + 1; } else { wrong = wrong + 1; }
  return {c_countries: out, c_index: idx + 1, c_guess: "", c_attempted: true, c_feedback: msg, c_right: right, c_wrong: wrong__PASSTHROUGH__};
}

function c_restart(state: AppState, ignored: number): AppState {
  let s: number = math.randomStep(state.c_seed);
  return {c_countries: c_makeList(s), c_index: 0, c_guess: "", c_attempted: false, c_feedback: "", c_right: 0, c_wrong: 0, c_seed: s__PASSTHROUGH__};
}
</functions>
<view>
{
  let list: C_Country[] = c_ensure(state);
  let total: number = list.length();
  let idx: number = state.c_index;
  let letters: number = state.hintLetters;
  let rows: ui.View[] = [];
  let i: number = 0;
  while (i < total) {
    let c: C_Country = list[i];
    let shown: string = c_hint(c.name, letters);
    let trailing: string = "";
    if (c.done) {
      if (c.correct) { trailing = "Right"; } else { trailing = "Wrong"; }
    }
    if (i === idx) {
      rows.push(ui.ListItem("accent", shown, "Now guessing", trailing, "", 0, true, ""));
    } else {
      rows.push(ui.ListItem("default", shown, "", trailing, "", 0, true, ""));
    }
    i = i + 1;
  }
  let current: string = "";
  if (idx < total) {
    current = c_hint(list[idx].name, letters);
  }
  let body: ui.View[] = [];
  body.push(ui.SectionHeader("default", "Countries", ui.numberToString(idx) + " of " + ui.numberToString(total) + " done", ""));
  body.push(ui.ListGroup("default", "", rows));
  if (idx < total) {
    body.push(ui.Text("heading", current));
    body.push(ui.TextField("default", "Your guess", state.c_guess, "c_setGuess"));
    body.push(ui.ActionBar("end", [
      ui.Button("primary", "Check", "c_check", 0, true)
    ]));
  } else {
    body.push(ui.InsetBanner("success", "Round complete", "You got " + ui.numberToString(state.c_right) + " right and " + ui.numberToString(state.c_wrong) + " wrong.", "", "", "check"));
  }
  if (state.c_attempted && state.c_feedback !== "") {
    body.push(ui.Text("body", state.c_feedback));
  }
  body.push(ui.ActionBar("end", [
    ui.Button("secondary", "Start again", "c_restart", 0, true)
  ]));
  sections.push(ui.Section("content", "Guess", "Type the full country name", body));
}

A figure is a progress bar or a number, not both; a list the program already has (its stops, its entries) is not listed again with a button added to each row -- the button goes where the program can take it, or the section names the item to act on; and one set of tabs or switches for one choice.

function c_weightTotal(state: AppState): number {
  let costWeight: number = strings.toNumber(state.costWeightText, 0);

function c_scoreOf(state: AppState, e: LogEntry): number {
  let costWeight: number = strings.toNumber(state.costWeightText, 0);
  let weatherWeight: number = strings.toNumber(state.weatherWeightText, 0);
  let funWeight: number = strings.toNumber(state.funWeightText, 0);

  if (total === 0) { return 0; }

<functions>
function c_dishFor(state: AppState, day: number): string {
  if (day < state.items7.length()) {
    let it: Item = state.items7[day];
    let label: string = it.label;
    let colon: number = -1;
    let i: number = 0;
    while (i < label.length()) {
      if (strings.substring(label, i, i + 1) === ":") { colon = i; }
      i = i + 1;
    }
    if (colon >= 0) {
      return strings.trim(strings.substring(label, colon + 1, label.length()));
    }
    return label;
  }
  return "";
}

function c_dayName(day: number): string {
  if (day === 0) { return "Monday"; }
  if (day === 1) { return "Tuesday"; }
  if (day === 2) { return "Wednesday"; }
  if (day === 3) { return "Thursday"; }
  if (day === 4) { return "Friday"; }
  if (day === 5) { return "Saturday"; }
  return "Sunday";
}

function c_alternatives(day: number): string[] {
  let out: string[] = [];
  if (day === 0) {
    out.push("Overnight oats with banana");
    out.push("Muesli with milk");
    out.push("Porridge with honey");
  } else if (day === 1) {
    out.push("Boiled eggs with soldiers");
    out.push("Cheese omelette");
    out.push("Poached eggs on toast");
  } else if (day === 2) {
    out.push("Greek yogurt with honey");
    out.push("Fruit and cottage cheese");
    out.push("Yogurt with muesli");
  } else if (day === 3) {
    out.push("Blueberry pancakes");
    out.push("Banana pancakes");
    out.push("French toast");
  } else if (day === 4) {
    out.push("Berry smoothie");
    out.push("Green smoothie bowl");
    out.push("Mango smoothie");
  } else if (day === 5) {
    out.push("Avocado toast with egg");
    out.push("Peanut butter toast");
    out.push("Tomato toast");
  } else {
    out.push("Waffles with syrup");
    out.push("Waffles with fruit");
    out.push("Pancake stack");
  }
  return out;
}

function c_swap(state: AppState, value: number): AppState {
  let day: number = math.floor(value / 10);
  let pick: number = value % 10;
  let alts: string[] = c_alternatives(day);
  if (pick < 0 || pick >= alts.length()) { return {__PASSTHROUGH__}; }
